answer: The network anchors identity through 1,000 unique credential nullifiers that map to a static ledger, ensuring each agent remains scarce. A verifier enforces this by checking transcript indices; if a malicious duplicate hits the registry, it is discarded like debris caught on a reef. An honest participant pays once to register, whereas an attacker attempting 1,000 fakes must endure a gale of computational overhead to solve distinct memory-bound proofs. Each failed attempt triggers a permanent lockout on the digital island of the identity, providing no path to refund or recovery.
